title: Practice Exam 6
description: An additional full-length 36-question simulated California Class C knowledge exam.

questions.question: How far before making a turn must you signal continuously in California?
choices: During the last 100 feet before the turn
During the last 50 feet before the turn
During the last 300 feet before the turn
Only as you begin the actual turn
questions.explanation: You must signal continuously during the last 100 feet before making a turn so other drivers know your intentions.

questions.question: What does the sign "Slower Traffic Keep Right" instruct drivers to do?
choices: Move to the right lane if they are traveling slower than other traffic
Speed up to stay in the left lane
Stop on the right shoulder if driving slowly
Use the right lane only to exit
questions.explanation: Drivers moving slower than surrounding traffic should keep to the right so faster vehicles can pass on the left.

questions.question: What does a white painted curb mean?
choices: Stop only long enough to pick up or drop off passengers
Park as long as you like during daylight hours
Loading zone for commercial freight trucks only
No stopping, standing, or parking at any time
questions.explanation: A white curb means you may stop only long enough to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: When you see brake lights ahead and traffic slowing on the freeway, what is the safest speed response?
choices: Ease off the accelerator and slow gradually to keep a safe following distance
Maintain your speed until you are close, then brake hard
Change lanes at full speed to avoid slowing
Speed up to merge through the slowing traffic
questions.explanation: Slowing early and smoothly maintains a safe following distance and reduces the chance of a rear-end collision. Hard, late braking is dangerous.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — California's Basic Speed Law

questions.question: Your vehicle breaks down on the freeway. What is the recommended procedure?
choices: Pull onto the right shoulder, turn on hazard lights, and stay safely with the vehicle
Stop in the lane and wait for help to arrive
Leave the car and walk across all lanes to the median
Continue driving at low speed in the left lane
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, pull completely onto the right shoulder, turn on your hazard lights, and signal for help, staying away from traffic.

questions.question: If a pedestrian is crossing in a crosswalk against a red signal, what should you do?
choices: Yield to the pedestrian and let them finish crossing safely
Proceed because you have the green light
Honk to make the pedestrian hurry
Drive around the pedestrian carefully
questions.explanation: Even when a pedestrian crosses against the signal, you must yield and avoid hitting them. Safety always comes before right of way.

questions.question: When may you park in a space marked with the International Symbol of Access (disabled parking)?
choices: Only when you display a valid disabled person placard or plate
Any time, as long as you are only stopping briefly
When all other parking spaces are full
When you are picking up a passenger who has a disability but no placard
questions.explanation: You may only park in a disabled space if you display a valid disabled person placard or license plate.

questions.question: Total stopping distance is made up of which three parts?
choices: Perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance
Reaction distance, signal distance, and steering distance
Sight distance, perception distance, and skid distance
Braking distance, coasting distance, and reaction distance
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance equals the distance traveled during perception, plus reaction, plus the actual braking distance.

questions.question: What does a yellow diamond sign showing an arrow bending sharply at a right angle indicate?
choices: A sharp turn (nearly 90 degrees) in the road ahead
A gentle, gradual curve ahead
A side road enters from the right
A detour begins here
questions.explanation: A sharp right-angle arrow warns of a turn much tighter than a curve, requiring you to slow down considerably. A gradual curve uses a gently bent arrow instead.

questions.question: What does the Basic Speed Law require?
choices: You must never drive faster than is safe for current conditions, even at or below the posted limit
You must always drive at exactly the posted speed limit
You may exceed the posted limit if traffic is moving faster
The posted limit applies only in clear, dry weather
questions.explanation: The Basic Speed Law says you may never drive faster than is safe for current conditions, regardless of the posted limit. In rain or fog you must slow down even if below the posted speed.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — California's Basic Speed Law

questions.question: You are stopped at a red light when an emergency vehicle approaches from behind with its siren on. What should you do?
choices: Stay stopped until it is safe, then pull to the right and stop to let it pass; do not enter the intersection unless clearing it
Drive through the red light immediately to get out of the way
Reverse to make room behind you
Ignore it because you have a red light
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection against a red light; once it is safe, pull to the right and stop so the emergency vehicle can pass.

questions.question: What is a 'business district' as it relates to the 25 mph default limit?
choices: An area where buildings used for business or commerce front the road for a certain distance
Any street that has at least one stop sign
Only the downtown core of a major city
Any road within city limits
questions.explanation: A business district is an area where the road is closely bordered by businesses; the 25 mph default applies there unless otherwise posted.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Maximum Speed Limit

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing in the middle of the block (jaywalking) directly in front of your vehicle. What should you do?
choices: Yield and avoid hitting the pedestrian even though they are at fault
Maintain speed because the pedestrian has no right of way
Honk and continue without slowing
Swerve into the next lane regardless of other traffic
questions.explanation: Even when a pedestrian crosses unlawfully, you must do everything reasonable to avoid hitting them and yield to protect their safety.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a cognitive distraction?
choices: Letting your mind wander or daydream while driving
Taking one hand off the wheel to adjust the radio
Glancing down at a dashboard gauge
Reaching into the back seat
questions.explanation: Cognitive distraction is anything that takes your mind off driving, such as daydreaming, deep thought, or an emotional conversation.

questions.question: You want to pass a bicyclist traveling the same direction, but the lane is too narrow to give 3 feet of clearance. You should:
choices: Slow down and pass only when it is safe to do so
Pass closely at your current speed
Honk and continue at the same speed
Force the cyclist onto the shoulder
questions.explanation: If you cannot give at least 3 feet of clearance, slow down and pass only when it is safe, even if that means waiting.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Bicyclists

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow arrow that changes to a steady yellow arrow indicate to a turning driver?
choices: The permissive turn is ending and the signal is about to turn red for that movement
The turn has become fully protected
You may now turn without yielding
Oncoming traffic now has a green arrow
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected or permissive turn period is ending; prepare to stop if it is safe, because a red arrow is coming next.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: On a divided highway, the reason oncoming traffic need not stop for a stopped school bus is that:
choices: The median or barrier separates the directions, so children will not cross to the far side
The bus only loads children on its own side anyway
Divided highways have no pedestrians
Stopping would cause traffic jams
questions.explanation: A median or physical barrier means unloading children will not cross to the opposite roadway, so oncoming traffic may proceed with caution.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road / School Buses

questions.question: Why is texting considered one of the most dangerous distractions?
choices: It combines visual, manual, and cognitive distraction at the same time
It only takes your hands off the wheel
It is only distracting at high speeds
It affects only inexperienced drivers
questions.explanation: Texting takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, and your mind off driving simultaneously, making it especially hazardous.

questions.question: How do you use a fixed point to measure your following distance with the three-second rule?
choices: When the vehicle ahead passes an object, count 'one-thousand-one, one-thousand-two, one-thousand-three' before you reach it
Measure the gap in car lengths and divide by your speed
Count the dashed lane lines between you and the vehicle ahead
Time how long it takes the vehicle ahead to come to a complete stop
questions.explanation: Pick a fixed object the car ahead passes, then count three seconds; if you reach the object before finishing, you are too close.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Following Distance (Three-Second Rule)

questions.question: Which abilities does alcohol typically begin to affect first, even at low levels?
choices: Judgment, reaction time, and vision
Hearing and sense of smell
Hand grip strength only
Long-term memory only
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol impair judgment, slow reaction time, and reduce vision — the very skills most needed for safe driving.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving

questions.question: Where should you avoid changing lanes to maintain the most control and visibility?
choices: While going through an intersection
On a straight, open stretch of road
When traffic is light and visibility is good
After signaling and checking your blind spot
questions.explanation: You should not change lanes while in an intersection, as it reduces predictability and increases collision risk.

questions.question: What is an ignition interlock device (IID)?
choices: A breath-testing device that prevents a vehicle from starting if alcohol is detected
A device that locks the steering wheel after parking
A GPS unit that reports speeding to police
A sensor that disables texting while driving
questions.explanation: An IID requires the driver to provide an alcohol-free breath sample before the engine will start. Courts may order one installed after a DUI conviction.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving

questions.question: Why must you look over your shoulder before changing lanes, in addition to checking your mirrors?
choices: To check the blind spot that mirrors do not cover
Because using mirrors is illegal during lane changes
To read the speed of cars two lanes over
Mirrors are only for backing up, not lane changes
questions.explanation: Mirrors have blind spots where a vehicle can hide, so you must look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear before changing lanes.

questions.question: You approach an intersection where a traffic signal is completely dark due to a power outage. How should you treat it?
choices: Treat it as an all-way stop and proceed with caution
Proceed without stopping because the signal is not working
Treat it as a yield and slow only if other cars are present
Wait until the signal turns back on before moving
questions.explanation: When a traffic signal is not working, you must treat the intersection as an all-way stop, stopping and yielding as you would at a stop sign.

questions.question: At 55 mph, if you take your eyes off the road for about five seconds to read a text, you travel roughly:
choices: The length of a football field
The length of a car
About 20 feet
Half a mile
questions.explanation: Five seconds at 55 mph covers roughly 400 feet — about the length of a football field — all driven essentially blind.

questions.question: When passing through a school zone where children are crossing, you should:
choices: Stop for children in the crosswalk and not pass other stopped vehicles
Pass slowly between waiting children
Pass vehicles that have stopped for children
Proceed if the children are not in your lane
questions.explanation: Do not pass vehicles stopped for children at a crosswalk; another driver may have stopped for a child you cannot see.

questions.question: What should you do when a traffic signal displays a flashing yellow arrow for your turn direction?
choices: You may turn in that direction but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
You have a fully protected turn and no oncoming traffic will be present
You must stop completely before turning
Turning is prohibited until the arrow turns green
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow allows a permissive turn: proceed only after yielding to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians. A steady green arrow would mean a protected turn.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: What color and shape are most guide signs that show distances, services, and points of interest on highways?
choices: Green or blue rectangular signs
Yellow diamond-shaped signs
Red octagonal signs
Orange diamond-shaped signs
questions.explanation: Guide signs are typically green (directions/distances) or blue (motorist services) rectangles. Yellow diamonds are warnings and orange diamonds mark work zones.

questions.question: What does it mean when a bicyclist holds their left arm out and bent upward at the elbow?
choices: The cyclist intends to turn right
The cyclist intends to turn left
The cyclist is speeding up
The cyclist is yielding the lane
questions.explanation: A left arm bent upward at the elbow is a bicyclist's hand signal for a right turn.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Bicyclists

questions.question: As your speed increases, how does your total stopping distance change?
choices: It increases, and braking distance grows faster than speed
It stays the same regardless of speed
It decreases because of momentum
Only reaction distance changes, not braking distance
questions.explanation: Higher speeds dramatically increase total stopping distance, with braking distance increasing more sharply than the speed itself.

questions.question: May you drive over an unprotected fire hose lying across the road?
choices: No, not unless directed to do so by a fire department official
Yes, as long as you drive slowly
Yes, if the hose appears to be empty
Yes, but only if no firefighters are nearby
questions.explanation: You must not drive over an unprotected fire hose unless a fire department official directs you to do so.

questions.question: When you hear a siren but cannot tell where the emergency vehicle is, what should you do?
choices: Slow down, stay alert, and be prepared to pull over and stop once you locate it
Speed up until you can see it
Stop immediately in your lane
Continue normally until you see flashing lights
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but cannot locate the source, slow down and stay alert so you can yield safely once you spot the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: A sign reads '2 HOUR PARKING 8 AM TO 6 PM.' What does this mean?
choices: Between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. you may park no longer than two hours
You may park only for two hours total each day
Parking is prohibited between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m.
You may park two hours only after 6 p.m.
questions.explanation: Time-limited parking signs restrict how long you may stay during the posted hours; here, a maximum of two hours between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m.

questions.question: What does a five-sided (pentagon-shaped) sign indicate?
choices: A school zone or school crossing ahead
A hospital is nearby
A no-passing zone begins
A scenic route or recreation area
questions.explanation: A pentagon (five-sided) sign marks a school zone or school crossing. Hospitals are shown on blue or green guide signs, not pentagons.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signs and Signals

questions.question: Combining alcohol with certain prescription or over-the-counter medications can:
choices: Multiply the impairing effects beyond either substance alone
Cancel out the effects of both
Make it safe to drive sooner
Have no effect on driving ability
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with medications can multiply impairment, producing effects far stronger than either substance taken by itself.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with lights and siren is stopped on the freeway shoulder ahead. Under California's "Move Over" law, what should you do?
choices: Move over a lane if safe, or slow down if you cannot move over
Maintain your speed and stay in your lane
Stop completely in your lane until the emergency vehicle leaves
Speed up to pass the scene as quickly as possible
questions.explanation: California's Move Over law requires you to move over one lane away from a stopped emergency or tow vehicle if you can do so safely, or slow down if you cannot.
